Its counts prove the three- and four-seed formulas recorded by Markey and the conjectured five-seed difference relation observed by Pfoertner and recorded by Markey. works.abstract_text: We answer Section 4, item 3 of Alikhani and Griswold's On the Integer Domination Root Conjecture by constructing connected graphs with domination root −4 and unbounded order. Joining r copies of their 33-vertex graph through vertices adjacent to leaves gives a connected graph on 33r vertices whose domination polynomial is the rth power of the original polynomial. A mixed construction gives examples of every order at least 35, with maximum degree seven and cycle rank four. We give a complete set-bijection proof, an exact finite calculation for the base graph, and the scope of the corresponding Lean declarations.

Their counts give a quadratic quasipolynomial of least period four, establish Stefano Spezia's conditional formula of June 8, 2024, and give the corresponding cubic ball count. We also prove that the proposed recurrences have the least possible eventual orders, six and seven. The same layer count proves the companion tcd formulas in A299287 and A299288. For arbitrary orientations of the tetrahedron–octahedron slabs, the tcd and tea counts are sharp lower and upper bounds, with sphere-count gap floor(n^2/8).

works.abstract_text: Question 9.1 of Johnson and Paparella, Perron similarities and the nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem, arXiv:2409.07682v4, Section 9, p. 27, has a negative answer for both polyhedral cones and polytopes. For every integer m >= 1 we construct a rational polygon with m+4 edges whose lift to x_0=1 and conical hull are closed under coordinatewise multiplication and contain the all-ones vector. Every vector in the polygonal lift is the spectrum, in a fixed coordinate order, of a symmetric stochastic matrix with a common eigenbasis. Neither set is the complete spectratope or spectracone of any complex 3-by-3 matrix: the diagonal entries and trace obstruct the required facets away from the identity. The five-vertex case already fails these constraints. Cartesian products give full-dimensional counterexamples in every coordinate size n >= 3. With boundary in the source's complex Euclidean space or its first-coordinate affine hyperplane, Conjecture 9.2 also fails: (1,0,...,0) is a boundary stochastic spectrum but is not radially extremal.

works.abstract_text: The all-length earliest-swapping conjecture in Section IV D 1, Eq. (41), of Kamin, Shchukin, Schmidt and van Loock (2023) states that repeatedly merging an adjacent pair with smallest maximum ready time minimizes total dephasing. The pathwise inequality also answers the exponential-dephasing question in Section IV D 5, for the same fixed-readiness swapping model: earliest swapping simultaneously minimizes expected dephasing and maximizes every expected exponential attenuation factor.

works.abstract_text: We extend Khesin–Li (2024), Section 8, by proving the operation-generated, decoration-free graph formulation of Conjecture 8.3 (page 23) and correcting the shared-output bound in Proposition 8.2 (page 23). For bipartite encoder graphs in one class, local complementations and input-edge deletions can be eliminated: output permutations and binary input-row additions suffice. The output cut-rank function is invariant under the original operations, up to output relabelling. At a bipartite endpoint this function determines the binary kernel, hence the row space, of the input–output matrix. For two inputs, the number of zero columns and the unordered multiplicities of the three nonzero column types classify the graphs. Their smallest achievable number of shared outputs is the least of these multiplicities, at most floor((n-z)/3) for z zero columns. The [3,2] matrix with all three nonzero column types has minimum one, whereas the published bound gives zero.

For the full positive-definite family obtained by adding c times the squared trace to the Hilbert-Schmidt norm squared, we show in every dimension at least two that principal-log minimality holds for all principal angles if and only if the trace coefficient is zero. Scalar examples give a strict failure whenever their eigenangle exceeds pi(1+c)/(1+nc), for c>0. Thus the proposed pi/2 input already fails in dimension three, and no positive dimension-independent spectral radius suffices.

We prove the exact classification: for 0 <= t <= 1, this matrix is determined, up to permutation similarity, among all similar doubly stochastic matrices if and only if t < 1/k^2 or t = 1. Using the classical integer-partition structure of diagonalizable doubly stochastic matrices with two distinct real eigenvalues, we obtain the two-eigenvalue part of the source's zero-trace question. When k >= 4 and 0 < t < 1/k^2, it has positive trace but lies on none of the segments in the conjecture. Explicit unequal-block matrices explain the sharp endpoint.

works.abstract_text: An elementary alternative proof of the cyclotomic specialization of Noferini–Williams Smith forms (2024, Theorem 3.11; 2026, Theorems 2.2 and 2.4) corrects Manju and Sharma's printed Conjecture 5.2 in Twisted Derivations in Algebraic Number Fields, arXiv:2412.03507v2 (9 April 2026), Section 5.2, p. 30. Its Gaussian witness is a specialization of Chaudhuri's 2019 quadratic construction. For distinct twists sigma(zeta)=zeta^u and tau(zeta)=zeta^v on O=Z[zeta], the outer module is O/(zeta^v-zeta^u)O. Writing h=n/gcd(n,|v-u|), its additive group is (Z/ell Z)^(phi(n)/phi(h)) if h is a power of a prime ell, and is zero otherwise. Thus, for n=p^k and e=v_p(|v-u|), the correct adjugate denominator is p^(p^e), not p^e; the printed test is integral for every derivation. Nonzero outer classes nevertheless exist for every prime-power twist pair. The same theorem settles the related determinant and innerness conjectures, including the prime-conductor conjectures in the authors' number-rings paper, and classifies conductors for which every distinct twist pair admits nonzero outer classes.

works.abstract_text: Using the cycle example of Mináč, Muller, Nguyen and Tân (2022, Corollary 2.5), we give a short negative answer to Nguyen and Tân's Question 4.17 (arXiv:2508.10348v1, Section 4.3, p. 19): Γ(Z/8Z,{1,−1}) = C₈ is prime, connected and anti-connected, with adjacency nullity two. More generally, C_n has these graph properties for n ≥ 5 and is singular exactly when 4 divides n. Extending Chen's binary polynomial construction with the tensor spectrum described by Sander, we realize every Hamming graph H(d,q) over a prime-power alphabet as a subgroup-unit Cayley graph of a Frobenius group algebra. For d ≥ 2, except (d,q)=(2,2), it is prime and anti-connected; it is singular exactly when q divides d, with nullity binomial(d,d(q−1)/q)(q−1)^(d(q−1)/q). These examples also answer Question 2.20 of arXiv:2603.21239v1 negatively. Finally, a short proof of Hendrickson's duality answers the supercharacter-axiom question in Remark 2.2 of the first source affirmatively.

works.abstract_text: Extending Glaisher's (1900) congruence to exact literal-remainder counts, we determine OEIS A222759 and prove Noe's growth assertion in its first comment (12 March 2013; revision 12, 2 November 2024). For every positive integer n, its conjectured count equals pi(floor(n^(1/3))) plus two explicit corrections supported below 27. Consequently, for every k >= 3, the count is at least k exactly when n >= p_k^3, sharpening the stated sufficient threshold p_(p_k^3). The same description determines A222760, including its exceptional relation to A222759 at n=5. We give a self-contained proof, the counts modulo p and p^2, and elementary consequences for the linked prime-counting entries.

More generally, cutting any cyclic perfect difference set at its unique largest gap gives this property. Every positive integer smaller than the removed gap occurs as an ordinary distance; the chamber inequalities therefore bound each retained adjacent gap below by its integer value. We give a positive integer dual certificate supported on exactly one row per retained gap; its matrix is unit triangular. The same argument gives sharp stability bounds. Explicit largest-gap examples answer Notik's analogous Bose and Ruzsa questions negatively.

works.abstract_text: The formula at line 12 of the pinned official export of OEIS A146304, revision 35 (February 16, 2025), conjectures that the number a(n) of inclusion-maximal nonattacking bishop subsets of the fixed-coordinate n by n board is O(n^(n-1)); extending Arshon's enumeration (1936, pp. 25-29) to distinguishable maximal completions disproves this growth law. For integers n >= 3 and 1 <= t <= n-2, prescribing occupied difference diagonals and recovering the seeds from maximal extensions gives t^(2(n-1-t)) <= a(n), while a staircase-board embedding gives a(n) <= A(n) <= B(n+2)^2, where A(n) counts all nonattacking subsets and B(j) is the jth Bell number. Thus log(a(n)) and log(A(n)) equal 2n(log(n)-log(log(n))-1) + O(n log(log(n))/log(n)), and a(n)^(1/(2n)) is asymptotic to n/(e log(n)). Each color has the corresponding one-color estimate. The largest coefficients have the same root estimates, and the proportion of placements with fewer than (2-epsilon)n bishops tends to zero for every fixed epsilon > 0.

The same argument gives the connected three-element fork as a counterexample and, by order duality, the corresponding negative answer for ω*-chains. works.abstract_text: We refute Conjectures 3.26 and 5.3 of Wang's Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups (arXiv:2509.18724v1, pp. 23 and 27). The commutative periodic monoid of finite subsets of the natural numbers, paired with levels zero, one and two under union and capped addition, has algebraic Davenport constant one over every nonzero commutative unitary ring. Its nongroup relative Davenport constants are unbounded. The finite submonoids with supports contained in {1,...,m}, m>=1, have the same algebraic constant, whereas the expression conjectured to equal it grows without bound as m increases.

works.abstract_text: For OEIS A344611, FORMULA (revision 27), we prove A344611(n) <= A160786(n) for every n >= 0 and give an alternative derivation of Manyama's (2026) convolution, complementing Andrews–El Bachraoui's (2026) strict-partition formulas. An injection sends a partition with nonnegative reverse-alternating sum to an odd-length partition of the next weight. We characterize equality, give an explicit lower bound for the deficit, and deduce monotonicity of the corresponding unrestricted count. The same parity analysis proves a shifted companion comparison, determines all plateaus of the negative-sum count, and corrects neighboring indexing and distinct-part descriptions. A bivariate series settles the linked ordered-composition interpretations, with their precise shifts.

works.abstract_text: For Chai Wah Wu's Conjectures 1–4 in OEIS A227244, revision 54, FORMULA (10 July 2026), we extend the bounds proved by Schott (23 October 2019) and Wu (10 July 2026) to exact least-prime-factor formulas, including all excluded classes. The values are 101 on 20n+16, 47 on 220n+8, and 149 on 72n+32 outside n≡2 (mod 5) and n≡18 (mod 55), where they are 101 and 47, respectively. On 168n+43 the value is 59 except at n≡26 (mod 55), where it is 47. A periodicity lemma and finite modular tables prove these formulas. We also characterize all indices with value 11 and extend Fried's (2025) Fermat-number counterexample to an exact criterion for Cloitre's totient condition.

works.abstract_text: The question in Xu et al., Section 4.2, page 12 of arXiv:2211.05563v1, asks whether the optimized witness bound equals the convex-roof geometric measure of genuine multipartite entanglement for noisy GHZ states. A strict separation holds for every party count n >= 3 and local dimension d >= 3 at an explicit noise probability. For three qutrits at noise p=3/8, the optimized witness bound is exactly 1/9, whereas the convex roof is at least 13/108. A biseparable overlap inequality and a positive-definite matrix give a two-observable lower bound. A written corollary extends the three-qutrit strict gap throughout 27/74 < p < 9/22.

works.abstract_text: We give an alternative proof extending Kang's (2026) refutation of Yang–Chu–Zhang (2015), Conjecture 1(ii), p. 15. For its digamma remainder family G_a, we prove G_a''(1/64)>0 for every a>=331467377585/629168992256, and G_a''(1/64)>1 for every a>=5269/10000. These bounds exclude complete monotonicity of -G_a on a parameter half-line containing strictly interior points of the conjectured range. We also give a necessary positive constant-coefficient condition in the authors' Problem 1 and characterize all its degree-four solutions as positive multiples of the function in their Theorem 4 at its endpoint.

works.abstract_text: Extending the two-sided destruction construction of Saxena, Chitambar and Gour (2019), we answer Yoeli and Gour's fixed-superchannel question in Instability as a Quantum Resource, arXiv:2602.18323v1, p. 5, Open directions, negatively: in every dimension d >= 3, dephasing-covariant channels are not exactly the fixed channels of any deterministic superchannel. Any completely positive Choi action fixing every such channel must be the identity. Two-sector pinching, including qubit complete dephasing, admits an explicit physical projection. Uniformity-preserving channels have the same obstruction in every dimension d >= 2. Explicit negative determinants distinguish linear projection from physical retraction and give a counterexample to the affine-set assertion in arXiv:2402.05474v2, Theorem 9.2.

works.abstract_text: For Zhan–Gupta–Hillery, Section 5, Conjecture 2 (2024, p. 10:11; arXiv:2306.17401v6, p. 11), we derive a strict-averaging counterexample from the complementary-layer Gram formula of Skotiniotis et al. (2018). Two different coefficient-square distributions and their whole averaging segment have the same Gram matrix and, for three sensors at theta = pi/4, the same error (14 - 4*sqrt(10))/27. We extend the earlier symmetric-probe calculation by proving weak convexity and the existence of a symmetric pure optimum without a symmetry assumption. This proves the companion Conjecture 1 and answers the source’s final question: one probe is optimal for both minimum-error and unambiguous discrimination at every detector angle. The reductions also apply to fixed unequal priors and diagonal impact patterns, without solving their general optimizers.

works.abstract_text: We refute the strong-dominance conjecture of Zoroa, Lesigne, Fernández-Sáez, Zoroa and Casas (arXiv:1608.00155v1, Section 8, Conjecture, page 30) for every number of labels N≥4 and every number of independent draws n≥5, with strictly positive rational coupon probabilities. For n=5 and p=(48,48,2,2)/100 and q=(50,46,3,1)/100, one has p≺q, but the probability mass under p is larger at two distinct labels and smaller at three distinct labels. These two inequalities exclude every real single-crossing threshold. The obstruction persists along a rational one-parameter family on a full real interval. A Taylor estimate extends it to every number of draws n≥5, and adding sufficiently rare labels gives strictly positive counterexamples in every dimension N≥4. The cumulative distributions retain the usual stochastic order. On supports of at most three distinct counts, that order implies the conjectured conclusion.
